# P1: A survey of teenage sleep research

Citation: Halvorsen, I. (2017). Annual Review of Adolescent Health, 8, 1-64.
Type: literature review of 212 studies

Abstract: Teenagers' body clocks shift later at puberty, so most fall asleep after 23:00 even when school starts early. The review finds that sleep under eight hours is common among 14 to 17 year olds and is linked to lower mood and more accidents. It sets out the terms and methods the later studies use.

My notes: Long, but the best place to start. Chapter 3 explains the body-clock idea in plain words.
